message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you set). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “UNO.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (numbers 0‑9 + two of each action card). 8 Wild cards and 8 Wild Draw Four cards. | | **Setup** | Shuffle, deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn** | 1️⃣ Play one card that matches either color or number (or an action card).
2️⃣ If you have no playable card, draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips a turn.
• **Wild** – choose any color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – choose any color; next player draws four cards and skips a turn (must be played only if you have no other playable card). | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, they win the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of all cards still held by opponents:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points.
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | | **Next Round** | Shuffle again, deal new hands, and continue until someone reaches the target score. | **Key Tips** * Keep track of what’s been played so you know when you’re forced to draw a Wild Draw Four. * Use Reverse strategically—if you’re playing with 2–3 players, it can help you avoid drawing extra cards. * Remember to shout “UNO” when you’re down to one card; otherwise you’ll get penalized. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak the scoring or add house rules for extra fun.
